subject: Social Media
title: The Metaverse Attention Trap
description: A quick win: understand The Metaverse Attention Trap.

hook.text: Meta spent $36 billion on a virtual world. The goal: capture not just your screen time but your entire environment.

buildup.text: VR headsets track eye movement, pupil dilation, and head direction. They know exactly where you look.

discovery.text: In VR, ads can exist in your peripheral vision, in the sky, on objects. Every surface becomes a billboard.

twist.text: Eye tracking data reveals more than clicks. Gaze patterns show desire, fear, and arousal. The data gets intimate.

climax.text: The metaverse promises immersion. That's exactly what makes it dangerous. Total immersion means total capture.

punchline.text: In VR, you can't look away. That's the point.

quiz.question: Why is VR potentially more exploitative than phones?
options: It captures where you look via eye tracking
